cues: Ninety grams of glucose is half a mole, which gives one mole of ethanol: forty six grams, or fifty eight point three cubic centimetres.
And one mole of carbon dioxide, twenty two point four litres at S T P. Recovering only thirty eight grams means a yield of eighty two point six percent.
text: Worked example ten point one. Ninety grams of glucose is half a mole, which gives one mole of ethanol: forty six grams, or fifty eight point three cubic centimetres.
